headline: MIROIR DISCOVERY GROWS: First Mining Drills 5.26 g/t Au Over 19.55m at Quebec's Duparquet Project
snippet: First Mining Gold (TSX: FF) expanded its Miroir discovery at the Duparquet Gold Project in Quebec with a headline interval of 5.26 g/t Au over 19.55 metres from 340.45m depth, part of the 2026 program testing the northern extension of Miroir. The result demonstrates the high-grade corridor is larger than earlier drilled and positions First Mining toward a resource update on a discovery developing within a historic Abitibi gold camp.

headline: TARIFF STALLED: White House Halts Refined Copper Levy Amid Midterm Inflation Fears, Futures Whipsaw $6.45–$6.50
snippet: The White House has quietly shelved its plan to impose tariffs on refined copper products, with sources telling Reuters that senior officials fear higher copper prices would spike manufacturing costs ahead of November's midterm elections. Copper futures whipsawed between $6.45 and $6.50 per pound on the news, while domestic copper producers gave back gains — the tariff premium that had underpinned domestic production economics is now in doubt, reshaping the near-term investment case for U.S.-focused copper developers.

headline: NEVADA SILVER MONSTER: Hycroft Vortex Hits 11.2m of 1,665 g/t Ag — 30.5m Interval Averages 780 g/t
snippet: Hycroft Mining (NASDAQ: HYMC) reported some of its strongest results to date from the 2025-2026 program at the Hycroft Mine in Nevada: hole H26D-6090 cut 30.5 metres grading 780.53 g/t silver and 0.49 g/t gold, including 11.2 metres of 1,664.80 g/t Ag. Brimstone confirmed up-dip high-grade continuity with 82.7 metres at 87.52 g/t Ag plus 5.5 metres at 1,345 g/t Ag to the north, and the Vortex system extended 150 metres west. The Vortex and Brimstone discoveries represent a high-grade core emerging inside an already giant Nevada silver deposit.

headline: 89 GRAMS NEXT DOOR: Hemlo Mining Drills 89.9 g/t Au Over 3m Just 50m From Ontario's Active C-Zone
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. (TSX: HMMC) released South-Rim Zone assays from the Hemlo Gold Mine in Marathon, Ontario: headline hole 6702608 returned 89.89 g/t Au over 3.0 metres, with two other holes adding 14.81 g/t Au over 10 metres and 12.97 g/t Au over 7.0 metres. Drilling has now defined 500 metres of high-grade mineralization within a 1.5 km interpreted South-Rim horizon located only 50–150 metres from the active C-Zone — meaning the new zone could deliver near-term, low-capital resource additions to one of Ontario's most productive gold mines.

headline: ALASKA BULK TONNAGE CONFIRMED: Tectonic Metals Extends Chicken Mountain Gold Corridor to 300m Vertical Depth
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSXV: TECT) reported the first 2026 assays from Chicken Mountain at its Flat Gold Project in Alaska: highlight hole CMD26-036 intersected 1.40 g/t Au over 30.00 metres including 4.58 g/t Au over 4.50 metres, extending a higher-grade corridor to over 300 metres vertical depth. Step-outs 1.2 km south expanded the drilled footprint by 200 metres. With 22,000+ metres drilled in 2026 confirming a Reduced Intrusion Related Gold System (RIRGS) amenable to heap-leach processing, a maiden resource estimate is targeted for Q1 2027.

headline: WNA LONDON: Nuclear Fuel Report Puts 2040 Uranium Demand at 150,000t Reference, 204,000t Upper — Nearly Triple Today
snippet: The World Nuclear Association released its biennial Nuclear Fuel Report at this week's London Symposium (September 9-11), projecting reactor uranium requirements to reach 150,000 tonnes per year by 2040 in the Reference Scenario and 204,000 tonnes in the Upper Scenario — versus approximately 67,000 tonnes consumed annually today. Global nuclear capacity is forecast to nearly double from 398 GW to 746 GW by 2040, with AI data centres, electrification and small modular reactors cited as the key demand accelerants. The report reinforces the structural supply deficit narrative that has driven uranium prices to multi-decade highs.

headline: NOVEMBER 10 COUNTDOWN: What Happens When China's Heavy REE Export Pause Expires in 60 Days
snippet: China's 12-month suspension of Notice 61 rare earth export controls — which rolled back the extraterritorial 0.1% rule and Foreign Direct Product restrictions on holmium, erbium, thulium, europium and ytterbium — expires November 10, 2026 with no dysprosium or terbium having reached Japan in 2026 despite the suspension. As the US-China trade truce shows strain, InvestorNews maps the three scenarios: a second extension, a selective reimposition targeting defence-adjacent buyers, or a full resumption of controls. For Western junior rare earth developers, November 10 has become the single most important supply-chain date of the year.

headline: 28,000 METRES DRILLED: Globex/Emperor Metals Targets PEA at Duquesne West After Full 2026 Campaign
snippet: Emperor Metals (a Globex Mining spinoff) has completed its 20,479-metre 2026 drill program at the Duquesne West Gold Project in Quebec's Abitibi region, combined with sampling 7,884 metres of historical core to create the most complete dataset in the project's history. Assay results are in for 42 of 66 holes, with structurally controlled thickened gold zones now better defined ahead of an updated 43-101 resource and a Preliminary Economic Assessment. The project sits adjacent to active Abitibi mines, making a PEA-level re-rating a potential near-term catalyst for the Globex royalty portfolio.

headline: 228,000 LONGS INTO THE FED: COT Positioning Data Shows Crowded Setup Ahead of September 15-16 FOMC Decision
snippet: The September 11 CFTC Commitments of Traders report, compiled by GoldSeek, shows net managed-money long gold futures positions at approximately 228,000 contracts heading into the September 15-16 Federal Reserve meeting — a historically crowded directional bet. Silver's managed-money longs have trimmed as rate-hike odds climbed to 90%, reflecting the metal's more industrial rate-sensitivity. The one-sided positioning creates a binary squeeze: a hawkish hike could trigger long liquidation toward the $4,050–$4,100 support zone, while a hold or dovish surprise could fuel a sharp short-covering rally above $4,720 resistance.
